title: 20260209 - Chaos to Clarity - Visualizing AL architecture for scalable Business Central solutions

chapters.title: Evolution from NAV to Modern Architecture
The Challenge - Interfaces and Bridge Apps
C4 Model Levels and Mapping to AL Architecture
System Context View and Diagram Principles
Container and Component Views with Design Decisions
Practical Application to Business Central Solution
Detailed Solution Hub Design Patterns and Testing

features.name: C4 Model for Architecture Visualization
features.description: A defined set of abstractions and diagrams created by Simon Brown for visualizing software architecture. Uses four levels - software system, container, component, and code - to provide clarity without ambiguity. Mapped to Business Central extensions, PTEs, and AL namespaces.
caveats: External to Business Central, from broader software architecture community
C4 containers do not directly relate to Docker containers
diagrams can be created with various tools like draw.io, not just original C4 notation

features.name: Bridge App Pattern for System Integration
features.description: An architectural approach for building connector applications between Business Central and other systems. Allows switching between different project solutions or ERP systems without losing data. External systems connect through interchangeable connector apps that decouple from specific project modules.
caveats: Described conceptually rather than demonstrated in early sessions
Presenter found implementation challenging in practice
interchangeability depends on consistent data models

features.name: AL Interfaces
features.description: A core AL language concept for building scalable solutions. Used in enum-based integration provider patterns with interfaces providing different implementations, supporting extensibility through solid principles.
caveats: Difficult learning curve for developers from NAV background

features.name: Architecture Diagram Documentation
features.description: Practice of documenting design decisions within architecture diagrams, such as specifying data formats (JSON, XML) used in system communication, to prevent confusion when reading code.

features.name: Code Architecture Reflection
features.description: Practice of verifying that implemented code actually reflects the designed architecture, and using tools to derive architecture diagrams from the code to map against the intended design.
caveats: tools to derive diagrams from code are recommended but not specified
Does not require constant diagram updates

features.name: Stakeholder Architecture Communication
features.description: Using architecture diagrams at appropriate abstraction levels to communicate with different stakeholders - system context and container levels for business executives, deeper levels for developers.

features.name: Solution hub module
features.description: A customization module that provides customer solution information including data about systems in use and projects being worked on. Developed as a PTE (partner-developed extension) without using app source apps.
caveats: developed as customization, not app source

features.name: EROC connector
features.description: A bridge app that sends and receives data from an external EROC system, connecting it to the solution hub module. Allows time entries from external project systems to be imported into Business Central.

features.name: Projects integration module
features.description: A module within solution hub that handles data flow between Business Central projects and external systems, allowing users to register time against project numbers. Designed to work with different project providers through interfaces and enums.

features.name: Enum-based integration provider pattern
features.description: Uses an enum to define integration providers and interfaces to provide different implementations. Allows new providers to be added without modifying existing code, supporting extensibility through solid principles.

features.name: Architecture clarity improves AI prompts
features.description: Clear architectural design with well-defined components and consistent naming conventions leads to better Copilot prompts with less ambiguity, resulting in more accurate code suggestions and faster automation.
caveats: requires clear data model and naming conventions

features.name: Structurizr DSL for architecture as code
features.description: A domain-specific language that allows capturing architecture diagrams as code. Supports C4 model notation and enables model-driven view generation where changes to the model propagate to all derived diagrams.
caveats: still needs export step to update diagrams
Requires manual creation of DSL file from diagrams

features.name: Copilot architecture validation
features.description: Using Copilot to review architecture diagrams and check if they follow SOLID principles, including dependency inversion, open-closed principle, and single responsibility principle. Can validate diagrams against solid principles and provide architectural feedback.
caveats: Copilot has concerns when it doesn't see all of the code

features.name: Structurizer playground
features.description: Web-based playground at structurizer.com that allows creating and visualizing C4 model architecture diagrams with zoom capabilities to explore different levels of the solution.
